channel.title: WasteDive – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from WasteDive – Bias and Credibility (wastedive.com)

item.title: States, cities sue EPA over endangerment finding repeal
item.description: A dozen cities and counties join 24 states in challenging EPA’s rescission of a cornerstone climate rule, which leaves cities “to bear the costs of hotter summers, dirtier air, and extreme weather,” Denver’s mayor said.

item.title: US textile recycling matures with AI and EPR
item.description: The fast-innovating textile recycling sector is looking for better ways to identify and sort feedstocks for both reuse and recycling applications. Startup Refiberd, along with companies like WM and Goodwill, want to make that process easier.

item.title: Michigan’s Titan Environmental closes after years of losses, lawsuits
item.description: The small, publicly traded company’s hauling assets and facility are now for sale after the platform was formed in 2023. A group of waste industry veterans, including members of the Rizzo family, had plans to grow in the Detroit market.

item.title: US EPA seeks comments on plan to remove pyrolysis from air emissions rule
item.description: The agency seeks public comments on a plan clarifying that pyrolysis is not a form of incineration. It’s a move the chemical recycling industry pressed for, but the agency previously declined to reflect in air emissions standards.

item.title: Maryland legislature nears approval of on-farm composting bill
item.description: The state’s Senate and House must each take a final vote on a pair of bills that would create a new grant program. It builds on previous legislation to promote organics diversion.

item.title: EPA should intervene on behalf of towns for PFAS in biosolids, filings argue
item.description: New amicus briefs filed in court this week argue that state and local governments are unable to meet the challenge of preventing PFAS contamination from the land application of sewage sludge.

item.title: EPA finalizes update to the Renewable Fuel Standard with more favorable biogas terms
item.description: The agency announced it has locked in requirements for the Renewable Fuel Standard through 2027. It tweaked its proposal released last summer, but kept in aspects like a penalty for foreign fuels.

item.title: Recycling Partnership CEO on navigating ‘really tough’ moment for recycling
item.description: Keefe Harrison shared how the nonprofit is thinking about the PET market crash, supply chain resilience, a loss in federal grants and the divergent funding needs of states with and without EPR laws at a MassRecycle event.

item.title: The one-man collection service advocating for vape recycling in Wisconsin
item.description: EcoVape Recovery offers small-scale collection services for vape waste. Raymond Tucker, a parks service worker and firefighter, also advocates for recycling outlets, infrastructure support and formal vape management rules.

item.title: Federal regulators scrutinize Noble rail plans; Juniper Ridge gets key approval
item.description: Noble Environmental is attempting a new waste-to-rail plan, but the Surface Transportation Board is requesting additional information. Meanwhile, the Casella-operated Juniper Ridge Landfill gets another approval from Maine.

item.title: New EU guidance on PPWR released less than 5 months from start date
item.description: Europen said the guidance “still falls short of providing the legal certainty and operational clarity businesses urgently require” ahead of Aug. 12. Implementing acts are still in the works.

item.title: GFL buys large Texas hauler Frontier Waste from private equity firms
item.description: The transaction includes nearly 650 trucks, 24 locations and a landfill. It significantly expands GFL’s footprint in the state, which is built on prior purchases from WCA and Sprint Waste.

item.title: Overlapping regulations help boost a Minnesota food waste digester
item.description: The forthcoming plant in the Twin Cities area is backed by a family company with ties to composters that believes anaerobic digestion can complement the region’s organic waste toolkit.

item.title: Maryland rolls out new paint stewardship program
item.description: The state plans to collect 350,000 gallons in the first year. The program comes a few months after Illinois launched its own PaintCare system and New Hampshire vetoed a plan for a similar program.

item.title: Casella acquires Boston-area Star Waste Systems
item.description: The purchase of private equity-backed Star is worth an estimated $100 million in annualized revenue. The company comes with multiple municipal hauling contracts and hauling locations, plus a C&amp;amp;amp;D facility.
